editorial.headline: Rice and Corn Flour With a Clear Bali Route
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10633 covers the manufacture of rice flour, corn flour, and corn grits, with national foreign ownership open and no Bali PMA block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10633 is a compact but important food-processing activity: the manufacture of rice flour and corn flour, including corn grits. The record does not stretch the category into trading, farming, packaged food retail, or broader grain services. Its center is production: turning rice and corn into flour or grits as an industrial activity. That narrowness matters, because the code is not defined by a brand story or a downstream menu. It is defined by the making of these flour products.

The activity is open across the full business-size ladder in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the code is not reserved only for one scale of operator. A small producer, a mid-sized processing venture, or a large industrial manufacturer can all sit within the same formal activity classification, provided the business being registered is actually the manufacture of rice flour, corn flour, or corn grits. For founders, this is the practical reading: the code follows the activity first, and the scale field tells you the registered size bands that the record opens.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is unusually straightforward. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100, so the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The source stated for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower cap in the record, no special minimum-capital figure, and no extra ownership condition to add. The honest national conclusion is therefore simple: at the national level, this activity is foreign-open up to the full percentage shown in the record.

The Bali reading is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. This code, however, is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. So the careful conclusion is not that Bali has a separate foreign-ownership percentage, because the record gives no Bali-side percentage. The careful conclusion is that KBLI 10633 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and, on the Bali field supplied here, not blocked by the Bali moratorium.
